title: Mount Abraham Formation
description: Lustrous, silvery-green to bluish-gray, fine- to medium-grained, white mica-chloritoid-quartz-chlorite schist and phyllite. Distinctive chlorite streaks and 1-cm rusty needles of altered kyanite are common

title: Mount Abraham Formation
description: Schist like CZa with minor garnet and magnetite porphyroblasts

title: Albite gneiss
description: White, light-gray- and green-banded, fine- to medium-grained, well-layered epidote-white mica-quartz-albite (+/-garnet+/-magnetite) gneiss, contains plagioclase and polycrystalline quartz porphyroblasts

title: Bull Formation, Bomoseen Graywacke Member
description: Pale-reddish-brown to light-gray-weathering, medium- and fine-grained, massive to thickly bedded, olive-green to gray, micaceous quartz-feldspar greywacke and siltstone, with coarse detrital muscovite, biotite and autoclastic slate chips

title: Coarse-grained amphibolite
description: Dark-gray, coarse-grained amphibolite and layered amphibolite composed of barroisite, epidote, garnet, actinolite, albite, chlorite, sphene, sericite, biotite and calcite

title: Fine-grained amphibolite
description: Bluish-gray, fine- to medium-grained albite-hornblende-epidote-actinolite (+/-garnet) amphibolite and quartz-bearing amphibolite

title: Mafic schist
description: Green, fine-grained schist composed of chlorite, actinolite, albite, and epidote with biotite, calcite, sericite, quartz, sphene, pyrite and magnetite, includes homogeneous, schistose greenstone, albitic greenstone, and massive banded greenstone

title: Biddie Knob Formation
description: Predominantly green, purple and purplish-red, chloritic hematitic slate and phyllite, massive to thinly bedded. Has rare thin beds of white vitreous quartzite and contains abundant chloritoid

title: Bull Formation, Mettawee slate facies
description: Greenish-gray to pale-lustrous-green chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite, and green and purple, bedded and mottled phyllite. Locally contains boudins and thin beds of limestone and pods of pinkish-gray to cream-white dolostone, and minor quartzite

title: Bird Mountain Grit
description: Dark-gray to greenish-gray and whitish-gray, massive chlorite-quartz wacke, pebble conglomerate and purplish-gray hematitic lithic wacke. Uniy is rich in fragmental plagioclase, phosphatic nodules, fragments of gray quartzite, and purple and green slate chips

title: Carbonaceous phyllite and siltstone
description: Medium- to dark-gray carbonaceous phyllite, gray slate, and metasiltstone, locally containing light-gray, medium- to thick-bedded quartzite and dolomitic quartzite (CZbq)

title: Browns Pond Formation
description: Gray to black slate, punky-weathering calcitic wacke and mudstone, thin limestone breccia in part equivalent to West Castleton Formation

title: Carbonaceous phyllite and siltstone
description: Light-gray, medium- to thick-bedded quartzite and dolomitic quartzite

title: Spangly schist
description: Silvery-blue, medium-grained tectonic melange composed of muscovite schist with minor amounts of chlorite, epidote, albite, and tourmaline, contains fragments and discontinuous lenses of greenstone, coarse-grained amphibolite, and talc-phyllite

title: Ultramafic rocks
description: Brown- to white-weathering, green, massive, moderately to fully serpentinized dunite and peridotite and schistose serpentinite, rusty-weathering, medium-grained talc-carbonate rock and quartz-carbonate (magnesite) rock

title: Nassua Formation, Rensselaer Graywacke Member
description: Basaltic volcanics

title: Dalton Formation, Dalton Formation undivided
description: Heterogeneous unit consisting of rusty- to tan-weathering flaggy feldspathic quartzite, tan-weathering quartz phyllite, and feldspathic quartzite

title: Dalton Formation, Dark phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to gray, rusty-weathering, well-laminated tourmaline-biotite-muscovite-quartz phyllite containing thin beds of laminated quartzite. Resembles dark phyllite of the Moosalamoo Formation (CZmp), with which it is in part correlative

title: Dalton Formation, Conglomerate member
description: Commonly tan- to yellowish-tan-weathering, coarse- to fine-grained quartz-pebble to -cobble, quartz conglomerate and schistose quartz conglomerate. Locally dark-gray biotite-muscovite-blue-quartz-pebble wacke to conglomerate. Occurs at or near base

title: Dalton Formation, Feldspathic quartzite member
description: Light-tan to gray-weathering, massive to thin-bedded, flaggy, tourmaline-muscovite-feldspar quartzite and interbedded phyllitic quartzite

title: Dalton Formation, Dolostone member
description: Buff, sandy, massive dolostone as lens in CZdph

title: Dalton Formation, Phyllite member
description: Rusty-tan to gray, thinly layered phyllite, tourmaline-biotite-muscovite-quartz phyllite, and quartzite mapped along western flank of the Green Mountain massif in the South Wallingford area

title: Dalton Formation, Quartzite member
description: Tan to whitish-gray vitreous quartzite and minor blue-quartz-pebble quartzite

title: Dalton Formation, Lustrous quartz schist member
description: Dark-gray to silvery-gray, tourmaline-muscovite- biotite-quartz schist and feldspathic schist and quartzite. Similar in appearance to CZhs of the Hoosac Formation exposed to the east

title: Fayston Formation, Albite schist member
description: Silvery-green to grayish-green, medium-grained albite-chlorite-muscovite-quartz schist with white albite porphyroblasts, +/-garnet+/-magnetite

title: Fayston Formation, Greenstone member
description: Dark-green, pitted-weathering, foliated carbonate-albite-chlorite (+/-magnetite+/-epidote) greenstone or amphibolite

title: Forestdale Formation, Phyllite and dolostone breccia member
description: Dark-gray to sooty-black carbonaceous phyllite, interbedded dolostone boulder conglomerate to breccia, and blue- and gray-mottled sulfidic dolostone

title: Fayston Formation, Carbonaceous albite schist member
description: Gray to medium-dark-gray, rusty weathering, carbonaceous albite-chlorite-quartz-muscovite schist, containing porphyroblasts of black albite. Unit resembles gray albitic granofels and schist of the Hoosac Formation (CZhab)

title: Forestdale Formation, Dolostone member
description: Lower part (not shown on map) largely cream- to beige-weathering massive dolostone and boulder and cobble dolostone conglomerate

title: Forestdale Formation, Dolostone member
description: Upper part consists of orangey-tan- to brown-weathering quartz-pebble dolostone and dolomitic crossbedded feldspathic metasandstone

title: Fairfield Pond Formation
description: Light-gray to light-green, quartz-sericite-chlorite (+/-magnetite+/-biotite) phyllite

title: Forestdale Formation, Quartzite member
description: Grayish-tan to light-gray vitreous quartzite and white feldspathic gritty quartzite

title: Fayston Formation, Quartzite member
description: White quartzite and tan to light-gray, medium-grained muscovite quartzite locally rich in magnetite. Resembles quartzite of the Tyson Formation (CZtq)

title: Fayston Formation, Schist member
description: Silvery-green to rusty-tan, fine-grained chlorite-quartz-sericite (+/-garnet+/-chloritoid+/-allanite) phyllite. Resembles green phyllites of the Pinney Hollow Formation (CZph), Mount Abraham Formation (CZa), and Tyson Formation (CZtg)

title: Fayston Formation, Foliated metawacke member
description: Salt-and-pepper-colored, medium- to coarse-grained quartz-albite-biotite gneiss

title: Hoosac Formation, Unvidided
description: Heterogeneous unit consisting mainly of dark-gray to medium-light-gray-weathering, white-plagioclase-studded schist, gray slabby quartz-rich muscovite (+/-garnet) schist and layers of dark-gray biotitic quartzite and metawacke

title: Hoosac Formation, Albite-quartz granofels member
description: Light-gray- to whitish-gray-weathering, massive to thickly bedded medium-grained biotite-white albite-quartz granofels, locally is a medium-gray, finer grained, more biotite-rich albitic quartz schist of gneissic aspect

title: Hoosac Formation, Albite granofels and gneiss-boulder conglomerate member
description: Light-gray, massive, coarse-grained biotite-white albite-quartz granofels like CZhab but containing boulders of pegmatite and of granitic gneiss, and disarticulated beds of albitic granofels as pseudoconglomerate

title: Hoosac Formation, Biotite phyllite member
description: Coal-black, lustrous, rusty- to non-rustyweathering, biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist and phyllite, containing lenses of white laminated quartzite as beds and discoidal boudins

title: Hoosac Formation, Conglomerate and quartzite member
description: Light-grayish-tan-weathering, biotite-muscovite-quartz conglomerate and pebbly muscovite quartzite, and dark-medium-gray blue-quartz biotite quartzite and schist

title: Hoosac Formation, Garnet schist member
description: Lustrous, green, ilmenite-chlorite-chloritoid-garnet-muscovite-quartz (+/-paragonite) schist resembles, Pinney Hollow Formation but lacks amphibolite. Aluminous schists at Devils Den and aluminous rocks of the Cavendish Formation may be correlative

title: Hoosac Formation, Dolomite marble member
description: Light-gray-, cream- or pinkish-gray-weathering, medium- to fine-grained phlogopite-quartz-dolomite marble. Occurs as thin beds in gray albitic granofels member (CZhab), locally contains beds of vitreous to bluish-gray laminated quartzite

title: Hoosac Formation, Chlorite albite schist and granofels member
description: Pale-green to light-greenish-gray, chlorite-magnetite-white-albite-spotted-quartz granofels and schist

title: Hoosac Formation, Garnet biotite schist member
description: Medium-dark-gray to lustrous silvery-gray garnet-biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist and feldspathic garnet schist, associated with CZhs member which it laterally replaces

title: Hazens Notch Formation, Undivided
description: Dark-rusty-brown graphitic biotite-muscovite-chlorite-quartz (+/-garnet) schist and gneiss, dark-albite porphyroblasts, large euhedral pyrite, and beds of dark-gray quartzite are common

title: Hazens Notch Formation, Greenstone and amphibolite member
description: Dark green, pitted-weathering, mafic schist to massive greenstone with chlorite, albite, carbonate, epidote, amphibole and sphene, and amphibolite with hornblende, actinolite, albite, chlorite, epidote, biotite, magnetite and sphene

title: Hazens Notch Formation, Schist member
description: Rusty-weathering, non-graphitic, sulfidic chlorite-muscovite-quartz schist

title: Hoosac Formation, Quartzite member
description: Light-gray-, yellowish-gray- to dark-dull-gray-weathering, biotite or muscovite quartzite, feldspathic quartzite, and pebbly muscovitic quartzite, commonly occuring as basal member or as layers in schist member (CZhs)

title: Hoosac Formation, Albite schist and granofels member
description: Rusty-weathering, medium- to dark-gray, black albite-biotite-quartz schist and granofels, marked by large spangles of muscovite and weathered-out pits of dolomite or ankerite

title: Hoosac Formation, Schist member
description: Lustrous, dark-gray to silvery-gray tourmaline-muscovitebiotite-quartz schist and steel-gray muscovitic quartzite

title: Hoosac Formation, Turkey Mountain Metabasalt Member
description: Dark green to black hornblende-plagioclase (+/-garnet+/-epidote) amphibolite and grayish-green epidote-plagioclase ankeritic greenstone, grades into epidote-quartz-plagioclase volcaniclastic wacke. Occurs as lenses at multiple stratigraphic levels

title: Jay Peak Formation, Schist member
description: Light-grayish-green, fine-grained, chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite or schist and quartzite, white quartzofeldspathic layers alternate with green chloritic phyllitic layers, locally albitic

title: Jay Peak Formation, Greenstone member
description: Green, carbonate-albite-epidote-chlorite greenstone

title: Moosalamoo Formation, Feldspathic quartzite and granofels member
description: Gray to dark-gray, biotite-albite-quartz granofels and flaser-bedded tan to gray feldspathic quartzite, latter resembles similar rock of the Dalton Formation (CZdfq), whereas the former resembles albitic rocks of the Hoosac Formation (CZhab)

title: Moosalamoo Formation, Magnetite metasiltstone member
description: Grayish-brown- to pale-green-weathering, well-laminated, magnetite-studded chloritic metasiltstone, near base contains magnetite-cemented quartz-pebble conglomerate and bedded magnetite quartzite

title: Moosalamoo Formation, Gray phyllite and metawacke member
description: Dark-gray, sooty-weathering, splintery sulfidic to non-sulfidic quartz phyllite and pebbly and gritty biotite metawacke

title: Bull Formation, Mud Pond Quartzite Member
description: Buff- to gray-weathering vitreous quartzite as much as 6 m thick, containing deeply weathered ovoidal areas of carbonate-cemented quartzite

title: Moosalamoo Formation, Quartzite member
description: Light-tan to gray, vitreous and non-vitreous quartzite and feldspathic quartzite and quartz conglomerate

title: Monastery Formation, Heterogeneous schist quartzite and granofels
description: Gray- to rusty-brown garnet-biotite-muscovite-quartz schist, gray albitic biotite-quartz granofels, light-gray to steel-gray biotite, minor epidote-magnetite-actinolite-chlorite feldspathic wacke, and chlorite-muscovite-albite granofels and phyllite

title: Monastery Formation, Quartztite
description: Beds of gritty feldspathic quartzite in CZtm

title: Netop Formation, phyllite and metasiltstone
description: Predominantly light- to medium-gray and grayish-green phyllite and metasiltstone

title: Netop Formation, albite-metasiltstone
description: Greenish-gray laminated albite-metasiltstone

title: Bull Formation and Nassau Formation, Bomoseen Member of the Nassau Formation
description: Pale-reddish-brown to light-gray-weathering, medium- and fine-grained, massive to thickly bedded, olive-green to gray, micaceous quartz-feldspar greywacke and siltstone, with coarse detrital muscovite, biotite and autoclastic slate chips

title: Netop Formation, Chlorite phyllite member
description: Beds of grayish-green vitreous quartzite and quartz-pebble conglomerate, and thin beds of chloritic wacke

title: Netop Formation, Chlorite phyllite member
description: Light-green to gray, lustrous, chlorite+/-chloritoid-muscovite-quartz phyllite and greenish-gray metasiltstone

title: Bull Formation and Nassau Formation, Mettawee Member of the Nassau Formation
description: Greenish-gray to pale-lustrous-green chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite, and green and purple, bedded and mottled phyllite. Locally contains boudins and thin beds of limestone and pods of pinkish-gray to cream-white dolostone, and minor quartzite

title: Netop Formation, dolostone and dolomitic quartzite
description: Dark-gray phyllite containing bluish-gray dolostone and tan-weathering to locally mappable gray-weathering dolomitic quartzite

title: Nassua Formation, Rensselaer Graywacke Member
description: Graywacke

title: Netop Formation, Wacke member
description: Bluish-gray, fine-grained metawacke and metasiltstone, perhaps equivalent to the Bomoseen Graywacke Member of the Bull Formation

title: Pinnacle Formation, Light-gray phyllitic conglomerate member
description: Feldspathic biotite phyllitic metawacke interlayered with lenses of quartz, feldspar, and gneiss-pebble to -cobble conglomerate

title: Pinnacle Formation, Cobble and and boulder conglomerate member
description: Poorly sorted, matrix-supported quartz- and gneiss-cobble to boulder conglomerate, locally containing quartzite boulders as large as 3 m, in a matrix of gray-weathering magnetite-calcite-chlorite-muscovite-biotite-feldspar schist

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Phyllite member
description: Light-greenish-gray to lustrous pale-green, chlorite-muscovite-quartz (+/-chloritoid+/-garnet+/-magnetite) phyllite. Chloritoid-rich rocks (CZphc) appear gritty owing to distributed porphyroblasts of chloritoid, locally albitic, contains minor beds of quartzite

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Dark-green to black plagioclase-biotite-hornblende (+/-quartz) amphibolite, epidote amphibolite, and ankeritic chlorite-magnetite-plagioclase (albite) greenstone

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Black phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to black, sulfidic biotite-plagioclase-quartz schist, commonly interbedded with or adjacent to amphibolite and greenstone member (CZpha), locally is a silvery-gray sulfidic biotite phyllite

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Chloritoid-rich schist member
description: Chloritoid-rich chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite schist or phyllite that appears gritty owing to distributed porphyroblasts of chloritoid

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Metafelsite member
description: White to pale-green, laminated to massive, epidote-calcite-muscovite-quartz-albite metarhyolitic gneiss or schist, a volcanic or volcaniclastic rock. Contains purplish gray feldspathic quartzite

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Feldspathic quartz schist member
description: Light-gray to gray-green, laminated, gritty feldspathic chlorite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist

title: Pinney Hollow Formation, Metawacke member
description: Silvery-gray, pinstriped, coarse- to medium-grained, blue-quartz-pebble chlorite-biotite-plagioclase-quartz metawacke, locally conglomeratic and rich in epidote

title: Pinnacle Formation, Quartzite and quartz-pebble conglomerate member
description: Light gray quartz-feldspar conglomerate and quartzite

title: Pinnacle Formation, Metawacke and phyllite member
description: Light gray, medium-grained, massive quartz-sericite-chlorite-albite metawacke, and gray to grayish-green magnetite-chlorite-muscovite-quartz schist, and phyllite or pebbly phyllite, locally rich in magnetite

title: Pinnacle Formation, Pinnacle Formation undivided
description: Gray, foliated muscovite-chlorite-biotite-feldspar-quartz schist, phyllite and metagraywacke. Blue quartz, conglomeratic horizons, feldspathic biotite phyllitic metawacke with lenses of quartz, feldspar and gneiss pebble- to cobble-conglomerate (CZpc)

title: Pinnacle Formation, Metabasalt and volcaniclastic rocks, undifferentiated
description: Largely carbonate-epidote-albite-chlorite+/-actinolite greenstones

title: Pinnacle Formation, Amphibolitic greenstone member
description: Calcite-biotite-sphene-albite-actinolite-epidote-chlorite greenstone with dark green porphyroblasts of actinolitic hornblende

title: Pinnacle Formation, Calcareous greenstone member
description: Rusty-weathering and pitted, dark-green greenstone with laminae and splotches of calcareous material, locally interbedded with calcareous metagraywacke

title: Pinnacle Formation, Feldspathic greenstone member
description: Olive-drab-weathering, dark-green, fine-grained greenstone with remnant plagioclase feldspar phenocrysts up to 1.5 cm in diameter

title: Pinnacle Formation, Metawacke member
description: Gray- to light-brownish-gray-weathering, massive to bedded muscovite-biotite-chlorite metawacke, conglomerate, and blue-quartz pebbly phyllite, wacke and feldspathic quartzite

title: Pinnacle Formation, Metawacke member
description: Heterogeneous unit consists of coarse- to medium-grained clastic wacke, beige-weathering dolostone, and quartz-rich dolostone

title: Rowe Schist, Amphibolite member
description: Very dark green to black, finely foliated biotite-plagioclase amphibolite to dark-green to light-greenish-gray, chlorite-plagioclase-ankerite greenstone and interlayered gray biotitic feldspathic volcaniclastic rock and feldspathic quartzite

title: Rowe Schist, Graphitic schist and quartzite member
description: Dark-gray- to sooty-gray-weathering, sulfidic, graphitic biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist, containing thin beds of dark-bluish-gray vitreous quartzite

title: Rowe Schist, Cooper Hill Member
description: Dark-gray or green, dull-gray- and rusty-weathering, slabby, well-foliated, quartz-rich muscovite-biotite-plagioclase-quartz schist, garnet schist, and splintery chlorite-chloritoid-muscovite-plagioclase (+/-garnet)-quartz schist, with minor feldspathic biotite gneiss

title: Rowe Schist, Biotite-plagioclase schist and gneiss member
description: Gray and light-gray-weathering, medium- to coarse-grained biotite-plagioclase-sericite-quartz schist and gneiss, commonly flecked with large cross-biotite. Locally contains coarse garnet

title: Rowe Schist, Garnet schist member
description: Mainly yellowish-green, lustrous, biotite-chlorite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz-garnet schist, distinguished by large garnets and coarse cross-biotite. Typical of rocks within the Stowe Formation elsewhere

title: Rowe Schist, Chlorite schist member
description: Rusty-gray- to yellowish-brown-weathering, lustrous, non-carbonaceous, well-foliated chlorite-quartz-muscovite (+/-plagioclase) schist

title: Rowe Schist, Garnet-biotite feldspathic schist member
description: Dark-grayish-brown-weathering, coarse-grained garnet-biotite-plagioclase-quartz schist

title: Rowe Schist, Chlorite phyllite member
description: Pale-green to dark-green, lustrous, magnetite-chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite and schist, highly tectonically laminated near larger ultramafic bodies (CZu). Unit typical of lustrous chloritic schists of the Stowe Formation, farther north

title: Stowe Formation, Schist and phyllite member
description: Fine-grained, lustrous, well-foliated, silvery green, grayish-green, and bright-green, quartz-ribbed and -knotted, magnetite-chlorite (biotite)-albite (plagioclase)-sericite (muscovite) quartz phyllite and schist

title: Stowe Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Dark-green hornblende-rich-biotite plagioclase (+/-garnet) amphibolite, epidote-hornblende-plagioclase-quartz amphibolite

title: Stowe Formation, Carbonaceous phyllite member
description: Interlayered grayish-green and rusty-weathering black quartzose phyllite, similar to dark carbonaceous phyllites of the Ottauquechee Formation (Co)

title: Stowe Formation, Schist and phyllite member
description: Same as CZs but with abundant dikes of metadiabase

title: Stowe Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Light-grayish-green, rusty weathering, carbonate-pitted, ankerite-magnetite-albite-epidote (plagioclase) feldspathic greenstone and interbedded feldspathic quartzite

title: Stowe Formation, Sericite schist member with metadiabase dikes
description: Quartz-sericite phyllite and schist

title: Stowe Formation, Large-garnet schist member
description: Silvery-green to grayish-green garnet (large)-plagioclase-biotite (chlorite) quartz-muscovite schist. Comparable to CZrgs in Rowe

title: Ultramafic rocks, Serpentinite
description: Brown-weathering, dark-green serpentinite

title: Stowe Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Dark-green to black, massive, medium- to coarse-grained, layered albite-epidote-hornblende amphibolite, possibly is a meta-intrusive. Exposed in the Worcester Mountains

title: Stowe Formation, Kyanite schist member
description: Silvery-blue, medium- to coarse-grained chlorite-muscovite-quartz schist (+/-garnet+/-kyanite+/-chloritoid); contains characteristic spangly muscovite and elongated knots of quartz and layers of pinkish coticule

title: Tyson Formation, Unvidided
description: Phyllite and metawacke. Shown east of Rutland

title: Tyson Formation, Albitic magnetite granofels member
description: Gray and greenish-gray, magnetite-chlorite-(biotite)-muscovite-albite-quartz granofels and schist. Similar to gray or green albitic granofels of the Hoosac Formation (CZhab and CZhgab)

title: Albite gneiss
description: White, light-gray- and green-banded, epidote-white mica-quartz-albite (+/-garnet+/-magnetite) gneiss with plagioclase and polycrystalline quartz porphyroblasts. Green, chloritic layers 2 to 10 cm thick also contain chlorite pseudomorphs after garnet

title: Tyson Formation, Albite schist member
description: Dark-gray to black, locally carbonaceous, rusty-brown-weathering biotite-rich quartz schist and dark biotite-albite schist

title: Tyson Formation, Conglomerate member
description: Massive to well-bedded chlorite-biotite(+/-albite)-quartz-pebble, -cobble, and -boulder conglomerate, feldspathic conglomeratic metawacke, and locally a dolomite-cemented feldspathic quartz-pebble conglomerate

title: Tyson Formation, Dolostone member
description: Largely massive, gray-, beige-, and pinkish-gray-weathering dolostone, beds of pebbly quartz dolostone, and pink- to orange-tan-weathering dolostone as lenses in phyllite. Contains beds of bluish-gray and whitish-gray vitreous quartzite. Similar to CZfd

title: Tyson Formation, Chlorite muscovite phyllite and schist member
description: Pale-greenish-gray to yellowish- greenish-gray, chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite and schist, locally contains beds of pebbly metawacke and magnetite phyllite

title: Tyson Formation, Quartz-pebble phyllite and wacke member
description: Gray to grayish-green, biotite-chlorite-quartz-pebble phyllite. Albitic biotite-(chlorite)-quartz granofels and wacke locally present

title: Tibbit Hill Formation
description: Metabasalt and minor metasedimentary rocks, massive fine-grained, dark-green metabasalt flows, pillow basalt, vesicular basalt, interbedded phyllitic grits, feldspathic quartzite, chloritic metawacke and basaltic tuffaceous metasedimentary rock

title: Mafic schist and amphibolite
description: Blueschist of amphibole (glaucophane, barroisite, actinolite), epidote, garnet, chlorite, magnetite, pyrite, apatite with quartz and garnet coticule. Green eclogite of garnet, omphacite, glaucophane, epidote, quartz, albite and white mica

title: Pelitic schist
description: Silvery-gray medium-grained schist composed of white mica, quartz, chlorite (+/-garnet+/-albite+/-glaucophane+/-chloritoid) local cm-thick lenses of coticule

title: Tyson Formation, Quartzite member
description: Gray to very light-gray, vitreous and nonvitreous, massive to thin-bedded quartzite, magnetite and biotite quartzite, and feldspathic quartzite, locally interbedded with dolostone. Similar to quartzites in the Forestdale Formation (CZfq)

title: Tyson Formation, Quartz phyllite member
description: Rusty-weathering, gray to grayish-green, chlorite-muscovite-quartz phyllite and minor beds of pebbly-quartz metawacke

title: Ultramafic rocks, Meta-ultramafic rocks, undifferentiated
description: Brown- to white-weathering, green, massive, moderately to fully serpentinized dunite and peridotite and schistose serpentinite, rusty-weathering medium-grained talc-carbonate rock and quartz-carbonate (magnesite) rock

title: Underhill Formation, Schist and phyllite member
description: Silvery-green quartz-muscovite-chlorite schist and phyllite, commonly with albite and magnetite, locally contains dolomite

title: Underhill Formation, Greenstone and amphibolite member
description: Carbonate-albite- epidote greenstone and massive magnetite-albite-amphibole-biotite-epidote amphibolite, light to dark green, epidote-chlorite-albite-amphibole schist; dark green, weakly foliated epidote-biotite-albite-amphibole amphibolite

title: Underhill Formation, Garnet schist member
description: Quartz-muscovite-chlorite schist and phyllite +/-biotite with garnet porphyoblasts

title: Underhill Formation, Quartz laminated schist member
description: Light-gray to tan and rusty-weathering, fine-grained, well-foliated mylonitic albite-chlorite-muscovite-quartz (+/-dolomite) laminated schist

title: Underhill Formation, Metawacke member
description: Local lenses of white to pale-gray quartzite, quartz-albite granofels, and quartz-granule chlorite (+/-biotite) metawacke

title: Ultramafic rocks, Talc-carbonate schist
description: Cream-colored to light-bluish-gray, brown-weathering, talc-carbonate schist and talc-carbonate-rich rocks

title: White Brook Formation
description: Buff to cream-colored massive dolomite and dolomitic sandstone, containing prominent zone of massive and specular hematite near top at Sheldon

title: Bull Formation, Zion Hill Quartzite Member
description: Light-greenish-gray to whitish-gray-weathering, massive vitreous quartzite, locally quartz-pebble conglomerate and wacke near the base

title: Cheshire Quartzite, quartzite member
description: Light-gray- to tannish-gray-weathering, massive to poorly bedded vitreous quartzite

title: Cheshire Quartzite, argillaceous quartzite member
description: Brown-weathering, gray to brown argillaceous quartzite

title: Cheshire Quartzite, phyllite member
description: Layers of dark-gray biotite-muscovite-quartz phyllite near top of Cc

title: Castleton Conglomerate
description: limestone conglomerate

description: Thin, light-gray beds of vitreous quartzite and crossbedded sandy dolostone. Unit discontinuous in southern Vermont

title: Dunham Dolostone
description: Dolostone, buff- and pink-mottled and massive, or light-gray, pinkish-gray-weathering, and massive to poorly bedded. Contains distinctive small pebbles and grains of well-rounded quartz, minor beds of dolostone-breccia and conglomerate occur near Rutland

title: Eagle Bridge Quartzite
description: Dull-gray, pitted, and bluish-gray dolomitic quartz wacke and quartzite distinguished by small pebbles and grains of dark-blue to black quartz, dacitic rock fragments, and abundant plagioclase

title: Hatch Hill Formation
description: Dark-gray to black, sooty- to rusty-weathering, splintery-fractured pyrtic slate and phyllite and interbedded bluish-gray dolomitic quartzite

title: West Castleton Formation, limestone member
description: Thinly laminated blue-black fine grained limestone, limestone conglomerate and boudins of whitish-gray weathering blue-gray quartzite

title: Monkton Quartzite
description: Reddish-brown, pebbly, thin- to thick-bedded sandstone, orangey-gray- and buff-weathering well-bedded dolostone, and reddish-brown-weathering dolomitic quartzite

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Carbonaceous phyllite member
description: Predominantly dark-gray to black, carbonaceous to highly graphitic, fine-grained sulfidic biotite-muscovite-quartz phyllite having silicic laminae

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Dark-green plagioclase-hornblende (+/-quartz) amphibolite and rusty-pale-green, punky-weathering ankeritic chloritic greenstone

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Black quartzite member
description: Dark-bluish-gray to black, fine-grained vitreous quartzite. Beds are as thick as 30 m or are thin and interbedded black phyllite

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Carbonaceous albite schist member
description: Tan- to dark-gray-weathering, carbonaceous, medium- to coarse-grained chlorite-plagioclase-muscovite-quartz schist and interbedded tan, gray, and bluish-gray quartzite

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Carbonate-bearing quartzite member
description: Heterogeneous unit consisting of ankeritic greenstone, ankeritic or dolomitic muscovite quartzite, bluish-gray calcareous quartzite, and pods of brecciated dolostone

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Feldspathic schist and granofels member
description: Gray and grayish-green, biotite-chlorite-muscovite-albite-quartz schist or phyllite and granofels, contains coticule, locally richly garnetiferous

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Coarse-muscovite schist member
description: Silvery-green albite-chlorite-quartzmuscovite (+/-garnet) schist characterized by coarse muscovite porphyroblasts

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Metawacke member
description: Tan to gray phyllitic metawacke composed of rounded to angular grains of quartz, blue quartz, albite and traces of detrital rock fragments in a fine-grained matrix of quartz, sericite and chlorite

title: Ottauquechee Formation, Schist and quartzite member
description: Light-gray to tan, rusty-weathering, laminated sandy muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist and tan quartzite

title: Parker Slate, Black slate member
description: Black arenaceous slate with dolomite horizons, interbedded dolostone and sandstone breccia in a dolostone matrix, and massive dolostone with thin sandstone beds

title: Parker Slate, Dark conglomerate member
description: Conglomerate consisting of round clasts of orange dolostone in a black arenaceous matrix

title: Plymouth Formation, Dolostone member
description: Light-gray- to beige-weathering massive dolostone and bluish-gray-weathering mottled dolostone breccia and conglomerate, passing upward into bluish-gray and buff dolostone breccia, dark gray phyllitic dolostone and limestone in upper part

title: Parker Slate, Dolostone member
description: Massive beds of white to buff dolostone

title: Plymouth Formation, Feldspathic quartzite member
description: Thinly laminated but massive appearing, gray- and brownish-gray- to tan-weathering flaggy biotite-muscovite feldspathic quartzite and phyllitic quartzite

title: Parker Slate, Sandstone member
description: Thin- to thick- bedded calcareous coarse-grained sandstone

title: Parker Slate, Sandy dolostone member
description: Sandy dolostone containing limestone clasts interfingered with sandy dolostone containing dolostone clasts

title: Parker Slate, Calcareous sandy conglomerate member
description: Conglomerate with dolostone and sandstone clasts in a calcareous sandy matrix

title: Parker Slate, Conglomerate member
description: Conglomerate with dolostone and sandstone clasts in a shaly matrix

title: Potsdam Sandstone
description: Light-gray, tan and dark-gray well-bedded pebbly quartzite, crossbedded vitreous quartzite, and local conglomerate

title: Clarendon Springs Formation
description: Steel-gray-weathering, light-gray, massive calcitic dolostone grading upward into darker, more fissile calcitic dolostone containing white quartz knots near top

title: Clarendon Springs Formation
description: Light bluish- gray to whitish-gray calcite marble within dolostone and beneath the calcitic marbles of the overlying Shelburne Marble

title: Ticonderoga Formation
description: Light-gray, yellowish-gray- to buff-weathering quartzose dolostone, pebbly dolomitic quartzite, and interbedded quartzite

title: Winooski Dolostone
description: Well-bedded dolostone weathering beige, cream, and buff, with green, red, or gray phyllite, siliceous partings, and thin beds of blue-quartz-pebble conglomerate and quartzite

title: West Castleton Formation, slate and phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to black, fine-grained slate and phyllite, interbedded thinly laminated bluish-black fine grained limestone, limestone conglomerate, and boudins (Cls) of whitish-gray-weathering bluish-gray quartzite

title: West Castleton Formation, Bebe Limestone Member
description: limestone conglomerate

title: West Castleton Formation, North Brittain Conglomerate member
description: limestone conglomerate

title: West Castleton and Hatch Hill(?) Formations undifferentiated
description: Black slate and gray phyllite exposed on Woodlawn and Tinmouth Mountains in Pawlet and Tinmouth Townships, after usage of Shumaker and Thompson (1967)

title: Frontenac Formation, Metasandstone and metapelite member
description: Thick-bedded, ankeritic, micaceous, and feldspathic metasandstones interlayered with subordinate dark-gray metapelite. Metasandstone beds are rusty weathering and up to 4 m thick, calc-silicate lenses locally present

title: Frontenac Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Garnetiferous hornblende schist and minor hornblende amphibolite

title: Waits River Formation, Carbonaceous phyllite and limestone member
description: Dark-gray to silvery-gray, lustrous, carbonaceous muscovite-biotite-quartz (+/-garnet) phyllite containing abundant beds of punky-brown-weathering, dark-bluish-gray micaceous quartz-rich limestone in beds ranging from 10 cm to 10 m thick

title: Waits River Formation, Mafic member
description: Massive, coarse-grained hornblende-plagioclase gneiss and granofels, finely foliated hornblende plagioclase amphibolite, and actinolite-epidote-chlorite greenstone

title: Waits River Formation, Ayers Cliff Member
description: Gray- to bluish-gray, fine- to medium-grained, thinly bedded calcareous metasandstone, quartzose metalimestone, and fissile, laminated calcareous metasandstone and phyllite

title: Waits River Formation, Muscovite porphyroblastic carbonaceous schist member
description: Dark-gray to coaly-black, fine-grained plagioclase-muscovite-quartz schist and metawacke, shown southeast of Springfield, in part correlative with staurolite-grade rocks mapped as Littleton Formation

title: Waits River or Littleton Formation, Muscovite porphyroblastic carbonaceous schist member
description: Dark-gray to coaly-black, fine-grained plagioclase-muscovite-quartz schist and metawacke, shown southeast of Springfield, in part correlative with staurolite-grade rocks mapped as Littleton Formation

title: Waits River Formation, Crow Hill Member
description: Gray quartzite and feldspathic quartzite, in part volcaniclastic and locally interbedded with amphibolite

title: Waits River Formation, Felsic volcanic member
description: Light-gray to grayish-green, chlorite-biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist and fragmental quartz-plagioclase granofels or metatuff

title: Waits River Formation, Garbenschiefer member
description: Rusty-brown to silvery-gray, coarse-grained garnet (large)-muscovite-biotite-hornblende schist and hornblende-fascicule schist

title: Waits River Formation, Irasburg Conglomerate
description: Gray- to bluish-gray polymict limestone metaconglomerate containing pebbles to cobbles of limestone, pelite, granite, and intermediate to felsic volcanic rocks, also locally occurs in the Northfield Formation

title: Waits River Formation, Quartzite and feldspathic quartzite member
description: Light-gray to tan, thinly bedded quartzite in beds 2 cm to 10 cm thick, exposed north of the Chester dome and south of Springfield, contains detrital zircon having Grenvillian provenance

title: Waits River Formation, Quartz-cobble and schistose metaconglomerate member
description: Light-gray, muscovite-quartz schist and quartz conglomerate and dark-gray carbonaceous, polymict schistose quartz conglomerate

title: Waits River Formation, Slate and phyllite member
description: Predominantly dark- to light-gray, lustrous, carbonaceous chlorite-biotite-muscovite-quartz slate, phyllite, or schist, contains thin beds of quartzite and only sparse layers of punky weathering limestone

title: Waits River Formation, Calcareous granofels member
description: Carbonaceous phyllite containing meter-thick beds of calcareous granofels. Unit occurs only in Massachusetts

title: Waits River Formation, Volcaniclastic rock member
description: Silvery-grayish-green to light-gray, muscovite-biotite (chlorite)-plagioclase-quartz schist and granofels

title: Averill pluton, granite and pegmatite
description: Gray to pink, medium- to coarse-grained garnet-muscovite-biotite granite and pegmatite, undifferentiated

title: East Barre plutons, muscovite-biotite granite
description: Gray, homogeneous, fine- to medium-grained muscovite-biotite granodiorite

title: Devonian intrusive rocks, binary and biotite granite and granodiorite
description: Binary and biotite granite and granodiorite, undifferentiated

title: Bethlehem Gneiss
description: Medium- to coarse-grained, equigranular to porphyritic, muscovite-biotite-microcline-plagioclase metaquartz monzonite, contains garnet, sillimanite-andalusite and cordierite

title: Black Mountain pluton of the Guilford dome, granite
description: Weakly foliated, light-gray to whitish gray, garnet-biotite-muscovite granite, minor pegmatite and aplite dikes (Dg)

title: East Bethel plutons, quartz monzonite
description: Very light-bluish gray to white, medium-grained, muscovite-biotite quartz monzonite, locally orbicular, commercially known as Bethel white and similar to the predominantly lighter-colored granitic rocks of southern Vermont

title: Compton Formation, Metasandstone member
description: Light-gray to tan, micaceous, locally calcareous metasandstone and slate or metamudstone in beds a few cm to tens of cm thick. Graded bedding common. Interpreted to be correlative with the Gile Mountain Formation

title: Compton Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Garnetiferous hornblende schist and minor hornblende amphibolite

title: Biotite metadiorite in unit Dgq northeast of St. Johnsbury, metadiorite
description: Biotite metadiorite in unit Dgq northeast of St. Johnsbury - Medium-light-bluish-gray, fine-grained, foliated and lineated

title: Derby pluton, granodiorite and tonalite
description: Light-gray, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, epidote-biotite-muscovite porphyritic granodiorite and minor tonalite

title: Derby pluton, granodiorite
description: Rim zone of granodiorite

title: Echo Pond pluton, granodiorite and tonalite
description: Light-gray to pink, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, seriate to porphyritic granodiorite and granite

title: Echo Pond pluton, gabbro and quartz diorite
description: Outer zone of quartz gabbro and quartz diorite

title: Echo Pond pluton, granite
description: Inner zone of granite

title: French Pond Granite
description: Pink to gray, nonfoliated, porphyritic to coarse-grained biotite granite, phenocrysts of potassium feldspar are as large as 2 by 3 cm

title: Fairlee Quartz Monzonite
description: Greenish-gray, pink-tinged, weakly foliated, coarse-grained to porphyritic biotite granite of the Fairlee pluton

title: Granite and trondhjemite dikes of Chester and Athens domes and W of CVT, granite and trondhjemite dikes
description: Garnet-muscovite-biotite granodiorite, muscovite-rich quartz monzonite and granodiorite, granite pegmatite, and aplite

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Hornblende amphibolite and hornblende-plagioclase-quartz granofels, interpreted as metabasaltic and volcaniclastic rocks

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Meetinghouse Slate Member
description: Dark-gray slate and phyllite containing sparse to moderately abundant beds of light-gray, fine-grained metasandstone and metasiltstone, 1 mm to 1 cm thick

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Quartz-pebble metaconglomerate member
description: Thin lens of metadiamictite with abundant dark-gray, pyritic, and calcareous metapelite matrix at the base of the Meetinghouse Slate Member (Dgm), south of Bradford

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Grit
description: Lenticular masses of metamorphosed quartose volcaniclastic grit and conglomerate, commonly having abundant dark-gray pelitic matrix interlayered with sandstone, pelite, and porphyritic rhyolite (Dgmr)

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Felsic metavolcanic member
description: Very light gray, fine-grained porphyritic metafelsite schist or granofels. Groundmass recrystallized to an aggregate of quartz, microcline, plagioclase, biotite, muscovite, and apatite. Relict phenocrysts of quartz, microcline, and plagioclase

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Thick-bedded micaceous feldspathic quartzite member
description: Brown to gray, noncarbonaceous quartz-mica schist and feldspathic quartzite in beds 50 cm to 5 m thick, gradational to Dgqs through interbedding of phyllite beds and decrease in thickness of quartzite beds

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Quartzite and metapelite member
description: Gray to light-gray, fine-grained, micaceous quartzite a few cm to tens of cm thick, interbedded with dark-gray, graphitic slate, phyllite, or schist

title: Gile Mountain Formation, Rhythmically graded member
description: Light- to medium-gray, fine-grained micaceous quartzite to dark-gray muscovite-quartz-biotite carbonaceous phyllite or schist in beds 10 to 25 cm thick, and dark-gray micaceous phyllite or schist containing beds of micaceous quartzite, locally thickly bedded

title: Granite and tonalite in sill-like bodies, granite and tonalite
