title: Ironbound Mountain Formation, Slate, phyllite, and schist member
description: Medium-dark-gray to grayish-black lustrous slate, phyllite, and schist containing sparse to moderately abundant 1-mm to 5-cm-thick beds of light-gray, fine-grained metasandstone and metasiltstone, commonly pyritiferous and calcareous

title: Ironbound Mountain Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Hornblende amphibolite and hornblende-plagioclase-quartz granofels, interpreted as metabasalt and mafic volcaniclastic rock

title: Ironbound Mountain Formation, Halls Stream Grit Member
description: Lenticular masses of coarse-grained quartzose volcaniclastic grit and cobble metaconglomerate commonly with abundant dark-gray metapelitic matrix (diamictite) interlayered with metasandstone, metapelite, and porphyritic metarhyolite

title: Ironbound Mountain Formation, Rhythmically graded member
description: Light- to medium-gray, fine-grained micaceous metasandstones that grade upward into subordinate dark-gray slate or phyllite, some rocks are calcareous

title: Knox Mountain pluton, biotite-muscovite granite
description: Light-gray, medium-grained quartz-rich, biotite-muscovite granite. Has distinctly more potassium feldspar and is lighter gray than rocks of the East Barre plutons

title: Kinsman Quartz Monzonite
description: Medium- to coarse-grained, potassium-feldspar-megacrystic, biotite granodiorite gneiss of the Ashuelot pluton

title: Littleton Formation, Gray slate and quartzite member
description: Medium-dark- to dark-gray slate interlayered with light-gray, fine-grained micaceous quartzite, in southeastern Vermont near the Vernon dome Dl is equated with DSwb and may be older than in Bradford area

title: Littleton Formation, Metamorphosed mafic volcanic rocks member
description: Metamorphosed mafic volcanic rocks

title: Littleton Formation, Metarhyolite member
description: White-weathering, medium- to dark-gray, foliated and laminated, aphanitic to very fine grained granofels to schist or metatuff, welded tuff, and lithic tuff commonly with a few percent mm-size quartz and microcline phenocrysts

title: Moulton Diorite
description: Dark-gray, medium-grained metadiorite composed mainly of secondary minerals such as saussuritized plagioclase, amphibole, epidote, chlorite, and calcite

title: Maidstone pluton, granite
description: Almost-white to dark-gray, locally pink, medium- to coarse-grained hypidiomorphic, granular, biotite-muscovite-microcline-plagioclase granite; accessories include apatite, sphene, pyrite, and magnetite

title: Newark pluton, granite
description: Pinkish gray to cream-colored, medium- to coarse-grained, magnetite-microcline-perthite-biotite granite

title: Nulhegan pluton, inner zone
description: Gray, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, biotite-clotted, hornblende-quartz monzodiorite, minor granodiorite, and granite divided into a western zone (Dnwz), inner zone (Dniz), and core of quartz monzonite (Dnqm)

title: Nulhegan pluton, main zone
description: Gray, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, biotite-clotted, hornblende-quartz monzodiorite, minor granodiorite, and granite divided into a western zone (Dnwz), inner zone (Dniz), and core of quartz monzonite (Dnqm)

title: Nulhegan pluton, western zone
description: Gray, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, biotite-clotted, hornblende-quartz monzodiorite, minor granodiorite, and granite divided into a western zone (Dnwz), inner zone (Dniz), and core of quartz monzonite (Dnqm)

title: dikes and sills
description: Dikes and sills of porphyritic and nonporphyritic metarhyolite of Hunt Mountain intrusive into the Albee Formation. Some contain xenoliths of the Comerford Intrusive Complex (Scd)

title: Stiles Pond pluton, tonalite
description: Gray, medium-grained, nonfoliated biotite-muscovite tonalite

title: Victory pluton, granite tonalite and monzonite
description: A western zone of medium to fine-grained, biotite-muscovite granite and minor hornblende-biotite tonalite and an eastern, more melanocratic zone of biotite-hornblende quartz monzonite like that in the Nulhegan pluton, and biotite granodiorite

title: West Charleston pluton, gabbro and diorite
description: Dark-gray, medium- to coarse-grained, massive, quartz-biotite-hornblende (+/-pyroxene) gabbro and diorite

title: Willoughby pluton, hydrothermally altered zone
description: Light-gray to pink, medium- to very coarse-grained, massive, miarolitic garnet-muscovite peraluminous leucogranite. Varies from a pegmatitic main zone (Dwmz) to biotitic granodioritic western zone (Dwwz) to inner hydrothermally altered zone (Dwhz)

title: Willoughby pluton, main zone
description: Light-gray to pink, medium- to very coarse-grained, massive, miarolitic garnet-muscovite peraluminous leucogranite. Varies from a pegmatitic main zone (Dwmz) to biotitic granodioritic western zone (Dwwz) to inner hydrothermally altered zone (Dwhz)

title: Willoughby pluton, western zone
description: Light-gray to pink, medium- to very coarse-grained, massive, miarolitic garnet-muscovite peraluminous leucogranite. Varies from a pegmatitic main zone (Dwmz) to biotitic granodioritic western zone (Dwwz) to inner hydrothermally altered zone (Dwhz)

title: Monadnock Mountain pluton, dikes
description: Dikes of granite, syenite, quartz bostonite, camptonite, aplite, and pegmatite

title: Monadnock Mountain pluton, essexite
description: Pyroxene-biotite-hornblende andesine gabbroic rock grading into quartz syenite

title: Monadnock Mountain pluton, granite
description: Hornblende-biotite microperthite granite, gradational into quartz syenite

title: Monadnock Mountain pluton, quartz syenite
description: Greenish-gray to pink hornblende-biotite quartz syenite

title: Cuttingsville stock, andesite breccia
description: Andesite breccia containing xenoliths of Mesoproterozoic gneiss and autoclasts of felsic alkalic and fine-grained mafic rocks

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, granite
description: Medium- to coarse-grained biotite microperthite-orthoclase-albite granite

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, hornblende granite
description: Hornblende granite occurring as small intrusive masses in Kas

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, syenite
description: Syenite-porphyrite to sericite-perthite-hornblende-biotite-syenite, contains minor fayalite, augite and quartz, occurs as a partial ring dike in the Little Ascutney stock

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, tuffs
description: Trachytic to rhyolitic tuffs, and breccias containing fragments of volcanic rocks having trachytic flow structure and layering. Interpreted as volcanic rocks of the edifice

title: Barber Hill stock, syenite
description: A small 0.5 km long, NW trending stock consisting of a coarse-grained alkali syenite core, a fine-grained quartz syenite border, and associated trachyte dikes (Kfd)

title: Cuttingsville stock, essexite
description: Essexite (alkali gabbro)

title: Barber Hill stock, trachyte dike
description: trachyte dikes

title: Little Ascutney stock, gabbro and diorite
description: Medium- to coarse-grained augite-hornblende-biotite gabbro infiltrated by hornblende and biotite diorite

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, hornfels
description: Dense compact hornfels consisting of recognizable but altered schists of the country rock only shown around main Ascutney Mountain stock

title: mafic and intermediate dikes, dikes
description: Predominantly mafic and intermediate dikes of diabase, olivine-augite diabase, lamprophyre, calcite amygdaloidal mafic dikes, alkali basalt, monchiquite and granitic, rhyolite, trachyte and foidal felsic dikes and spherulitic trachyte dikes

title: Cuttingsville stock, syenite
description: Nepheline and sodalite syenite, hornblende syenite

title: Ascutney Mountain stock, paisanite dike
description: Fine-grained syenitic dike similar to spherulitic dikes found within the plutons and in the adjacent country rocks

title: Cuttingsville stock, quartz syenite
description: Quartz syenite

title: Albee Formation, Metasandstone and metasiltstone member
description: Light-gray to greenish-gray, white-weathering, fine-grained feldspathic metasandstone and metasiltstone, and light-gray to greenish-gray to dark-gray phyllite. Lesser amounts of quartzite. Rare calc-silicate nodules. Locally sulfidic. Pinstriping is common

title: Albee Formation, Iron formation member
description: Ironstone, magnetite-rich rock and coticule

title: Albee Formation, Magnetite-rich areas
description: Magnetite-rich areas in Albee Formation OCal shown as overprint

title: Albee Formation, Slate and phyllite member
description: Commonly sulfidic and rusty weathering. Indistinguishable from the Scarritt Member, but crops out in small areas

title: Albee Formation, Scarrritt Member
description: Dark-gray slate interlayered with thin beds of light-gray, fine-grained micaceous and feldspathic metasandstone

title: Gorge Formation
description: Dolomite and dolomite breccia composed of angular clasts of dolostone, sandstone, and chert in buff to gray quartzose dolostone

title: Skeels Corners Slate, Black slate member
description: Laminated black slate with thin orange dolostone beds, includes massive dolostones mapped as Saxe Brook Formation by others in the Highgate area

title: Skeels Corners Slate, Limestone matrix conglomerate member
description: Limestone and sandstone clasts in a limestone matrix, interbedded with sandstone

title: Skeels Corners Slate, Sandy matrix conglomerate member
description: Limestone and sandstone clasts in a quartz sand matrix

title: Sweetsburg Formation
description: Black to gray, graphitic, quartzose phyllite and schist, with tan-weathering layers and pods of gray dolostone and black quartzite

title: Whitehall Formation
description: Predominantly light-gray and pinkish-gray, coarse-grained dolostone and cherty dolostone, containing layers of gray limestone (Ocwl)

title: Whitehall Formation
description: Gray limestone

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Undivided
description: Heterogeneous unit of metamorphosed volcanic, volcaniclastic, and sedimentary rocks dominated by tuff to tuff-breccia of basalt to sodic rhyolite. Sedimentary protoliths include gray sulfidic shale, ironstone, siltstone, graywacke, volcanic conglomerate, and rare limestone

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Meta-andesitic and metabasaltic tuff member
description: Dark-greenish-gray to medium-bluish-gray metamorphosed andesitic and basaltic tuff, crystal tuff, and tuff breccia, minor pillow lava. Commonly contains plagioclase and (or) altered mafic phenocrysts

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Dolomite and pelite member
description: Siliceous and argillaceous dolomite and calcareous pelite

title: Austin Glen Graywacke
description: Light-gray, tan weathering, mica-speckled, massive to thin-bedded quartz-plagioclase wacke interbedded with dark gray carbonaceous slate. Conatins autoclastic chips of gray slate, fragments of volcanics and clasts of gray quartz and oligoclase

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Metasiltstone, phyllite and metawacke member
description: Medium-light-bluish-gray, medium-bluish-gray, medium-dark-gray, to medium-dark-greenish-gray metasiltstone and phyllite and medium-gray feldspathic metawacke. Purple tinge common, coticule and magnetite locally abundant

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Sulfidic slate and phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to grayish-black, rusty-weathering, sulfidic slate and phyllite interlayered with felsic tuffs and minor sandy rocks, locally forms the base of the Ammonoosuc Volcanics

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Metarhyolite tuff member
description: Greenish-gray, light-bluish-gray, or medium-bluish-gray metarhyolite tuff, lapilli tuff, tuff breccia, and lava. Generally porphyritic with 5 to 20 percent plagioclase and, in some places, quartz phenocrysts

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Coarsely porphyritic metarhyolite tuff member
description: Coarsely porphyritic, greenish-gray, light-bluish-gray, or medium-bluish-gray metarhyolite tuff, lapilli tuff, and tuff breccia. Quartz and plagioclase phenocrysts commonly as large as 5 mm

title: Ammonoosuc Volcanics, Metamorphosed aphyric rhyolite tuff member
description: Metamorphosed aphyric rhyolite tuff

title: Bascom Formation
description: Interbedded orangey-tan to buff-weathering dolostone and bluish-gray to gray mottled dolomitic limestone or calcite marble and calcareous sandstone

title: Beekmantown Group undivided
description: Gray limestones, fossiliferous limestones, and dolostones

title: Biotite quartz diorite gneiss of Vernon dome
description: Light-gray, well-foliated subporphyritic biotite (+/-hornblende)-quartz diorite and trondhjemite gneiss, forms sills in overlying Ammonoosuc Volcanics

title: Black River Group undivided
description: Thin-bedded to massive dolostone, sandy dolostone, and light-gray limestone, vertical burrows in basal beds, upper beds fossiliferous with black chert

title: Walloomsac Formation, Vesicular basalt igneous breccia
description: Vesicular basalt igneous breccia in the Walloomsac Formation perhaps intrusive

title: Chipman Formation, Beldens Member
description: Light-gray to creamy-white-weathering fine grained limestone, orangey-buff-weathering dolostone, and reddish streaked (hematite) calcite marble

title: Chipman Formation, Bridport Member
description: Thickly bedded, beeswax-scored, orangey-beige-weathering, yellowish-gray to light-bluish-gray dolostone, dark-gray dolostone and minor beds of bluish-gray limestone. Transitions to Beldens Mbr.. Equivalent to Providence Island Dolostone (Ofcpi)

title: Chipman Formation, Buchards Member
description: Light-bluish-gray mottled dolomitic limestone

title: Chazy Group undivided
description: Dark- to light-gray, massively bedded fossiliferous limestone and calcareous sandstone

title: Cram Hill Formation, Gray quartz schist member
description: Rusty-grayish-brown-weathering, locally splintery-fractured, dark-gray to steel-gray biotite-quartz-feldspathic schist and quartzite and interbedded carbonaceous, small-garnet papery muscovite phyllite and schist similar to Ochs

title: Cram Hill Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Light-greenish-gray, feldspathic chlorite-actinolite greenstone and bedded andesitic to basaltic tuff and amphibolite, associated with ironstone, coticule, and minor pods of dolostone

title: Cram Hill Formation of the Newport Center area, Coburn Hill Metabasalt Member
description: Light-green, fine- to medium-grained, massive carbonate-biotite-quartz-sphene-chlorite-actinolite-epidote greenstone with deformed pillows, interfingers with the Umbrella Hill Conglomerate Member (Ochuc) and with phyllite-chip conglomerate (Ochsb)

title: Cumberland Head Formation
description: Interbedded graded bioclastic limestone, bluish-gray calcareous shale, and laminated shale

title: Cram Hill Formation, Granofels member
description: Dark-medium-gray biotite-plagioclase-quartz granofels and and grayish-green chlorite-plagioclase-quartz granofels, contains thin layers of ankerite-epidote greenstone, ankerite-spotted feldspathic granofels, and coticule. Locally hornblende rich at higher metamorphic grade

title: Cram Hill Formation, Feldspathic schist and granofels member
description: Medium-dark-gray to dark-gray, rusty-weathering garnet-biotite-muscovite-quartz-plagioclase schist and granofels, has coarse spangles of muscovite and locally is kyanite-rich

title: Cram Hill Formation, Felsic volcanic member
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray, fine-grained sericite-quartz-phenocrystic phyllitic metatuff and whitish pyritiferous soda-rhyolite metatuff

title: Cram Hill Formation, Ironstone, quartzite, and coticule member
description: Dark-gray- to sooty-black-weathering siliceous ironstone, magnetite quartzite, garnet quartzite, rusty weathering amphibolite, coticule, and pods of orangey-gray to pinkish-gray-weathering dolostone

title: Cram Hill Formation of the Newport Center area, Phyllite member
description: Gray to silvery-green, sericite-chlorite-quartz phyllite with thin beds of rusty-weathering, pearly-white, fine-grained granofels. Interlayered with Ochuc and Ochsb at the contacts. Mapped locally in the Albany area

title: Cram Hill Formation of the Newport Center area, Phyllite and quartzite member
description: Light-gray to tan, rusty-weathering, fine-grained quartz-sericite-chlorite-albite phyllite, quartzite, and flinty sulfidic granofels, with thin layers of felsite, conglomerate, and breccia in the vicinity of Coburn Hill

title: Cram Hill Formation, Quartzite and quartz-pebble conglomerate member
description: Tan- to gray-weathering, quartz-pebble and -cobble conglomerate, feldspathic quartzite and associated slabby, rusty-weathering amphibolite and coticule

title: Cram Hill Formation, Carbonaceous schist member
description: Light-grayish-brown- to tan-weathering, medium-dark-gray, fine-grained garnet (small)-biotite-muscovite phyllite and schist. Similar to phyllite facies (Omwh) in the Whetstone Hill Member of the Moretown Formation

title: Cram Hill Formation of the Newport Center area, Phyllite-chip conglomerate and slate conglomerate member
description: Dark-gray, carbonaceous garnet-pyrite-sericite-chlorite-quartz phyllite with clasts of siltstone, phyllite, quartzite, and dark-gray slate breccia interbedded with Coburn Hill Metabasalt Member. Correlative with the St. Daniel Group of Quebec

title: Cram Hill Formation, undivided member
description: Dark-gray to grayish-green quartz-chlorite-(biotite)-muscovite phyllite, contains beds of dark-gray metasiltstone, quartzite, dark-bluish-gray vitreous quartzite, sericite phyllite (felsic tuffs), cobble to boulder conglomerate, and greenstone

title: Cram Hill Formation of the Newport Center area, Umbrella Hill Conglomerate Member
description: Quartz-pebble and phyllitic-fragment conglomerate, and tan to gray phyllite

title: Cram Hill Formation, Felsic and intermediate metavolcanic member
description: Dark-gray and white layered metadacite and meta-andesite, gray- to tan-weathering blue-quartz phenocrystic metadacitic agglomerate, and grayish-green fragmental metadacitic and meta-andesite breccia

title: Crown Point Formation
description: Gray, massively bedded fossiliferous limestone

title: Cutting Dolostone
description: Gray, thinly bedded dolomitic sandstone, grading upward into dolomitic limestone or mottled dolomitic marble

title: Chipman Formation, Weybridge Member
description: Light-gray to cream-colored fine-grained calcite marble, and thin dolomitic layers, locally crossbedded, may occur as lenses at several positions within the Beldens Member

title: Day Point Formation
description: Gray, thin-bedded to massive sandstone and fossiliferous limestone

title: Fort Ann Formation
description: Shown only in New York State - Medium- to dark-gray and mottled, medium- to thick-bedded dolomitic limestone and buff weathering dolostone

title: Fort Cassin Formation
description: Shown locally from Whitehall, NY to Orwell, VT. Laterally equivalent to Providence Island Dolostone

title: Fort Cassin Formation, Root Pond Quartzite Member
description: Light-gray, to tannish-white, well-bedded and vitreous steel-gray quartzite interbedded with orangey-tan- and beige-weathering dolostone and thin beds of fossiliferous limestone

title: Fort Cassin Formation, Scotia Limestone Member
description: Light-gray, fine-grained, and dark gray, fossiliferous, platy bluish-gray limestone. Contains upper Ibexian to lower Whiterockian conodonts at the type locality near Sciota School House, in the Benson quadrangle

title: Fort Cassin Formation, Ward Siltstone Member
description: Light-tan to gray, thinly bedded and crossbedded, calcareous and dolomitic siltstone and quartzite in beds similar to the quartzite of the Root Pond Member

title: Ira and Hortonville Formations, Forbes Hill conglomerate and breccia
description: Black slate containing angular to irregular chips of greenish-gray to yellowish-gray slate, quartz wacke, and limestone. Interpreted by Zen (1961) as sedimentary wildflysch

title: Glens Falls Limestone
description: Dark-bluish-gray-weathering, thinly bedded dark-gray to black granular limestone, locally grades upwards into sooty-weathering shaly limestone beds rich in fragments of the trilobite Cryptolithus

title: Great Meadows Formation
description: Light-gray, medium-grained, medium- to thick-bedded dolostone, locally cherty, contains lens of light-gray weathering fossiliferous limestone (Ogml)

title: Great Meadows Formation
description: Light-gray weathering fossiliferous limestone

title: Great Meadows Formation, Winchell Creek Member
description: Tan-weathering, gray, well-bedded and crossbedded laminated quartzite and dolostone, sandy beds weather to a woody-grained surface texture

title: Hortonville Formation
description: Dark-gray siliceous shale and phyllite, containing thin beds of bluish-gray argillaceous limestone and minor beds of gray to tan quartzite, grades into limey shales of the Stony Point Formation

title: Hathaway Formation
description: Clasts of limestone, dolostone, sandstone, and chert within beds of black shale and chert

title: Hortonville Formation
description: Polymict limestone and dolostone-clast conglomerate

title: Highgate Formation
description: Banded limestone and calcareous slate with local lenses of conglomerate composed of limestone, sandstone and dolostone clasts in a sandy limestone matrix

title: Highlandcroft Granodiorite
description: Medium-greenish-gray to dark-greenish-gray, medium-grained, foliated metamorphosed granite, granodiorite, and tonalite containing quartz, microcline, saussuritized plagioclase, hornblende, biotite (chlorite alteration), and secondary calcite and sericite

title: Hortonville Formation
description: Near base (of formation) bluish-gray, granular, smooth-weathering fossiliferous limestone

title: Ira Formation
description: Same description as Hortonville - Dark-gray siliceous shale and phyllite, containing thin beds of bluish-gray argillaceous limestone and minor beds of gray to tan quartzite, grades into limey shales

title: Iberville Formation
description: Dark-gray shale with thin discontinuous beds of crossbedded and graded dolomitic siltstone

title: Ira Formation
description: Basal limestone member - locally referred to as Whipple Marble Member

title: Ira Formation
description: Polymict limestone conglomerate

title: Indian River Slate
description: Deep-maroon and bluish-green-weathering, well-bedded and variegated slate, contains minor cm-thick, white-weathering red and bluish-black cherty layers characteristic of the Mount Merino Formation. Has graptolites of C. bicornis Biozone (Berry, 1961)

title: Joslin Turn Tonalite
description: Greenish-gray to light-brownish-gray, medium-grained, weakly foliated metamorphosed tonalite. Primary minerals include quartz, plagioclase, biotite, magnetite, pyrite, and apatite; secondary minerals include chlorite, epidote, sericite, and calcite

title: Lost Nation granite
description: Foliated biotite and (or) hornblende granite, locally diorite and lesser amounts of gabbro. Where present, potassium feldspar is microcline. Contact aureole is in the Albee Formation

title: Moretown Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Includes light-pale-green chloritic ankeritic greenstone, black fine-grained hornblende plagioclase (+/-garnet+/-epidote) amphibolite, and hornblende-spotted dioritic amphibolite (Omd)

title: Moretown Formation, Carbonaceous and sulfidic schist member
description: Rusty-weathering, dark-gray biotite-muscovite-quartz (+/-garnet) schist, carbonaceous schist, and gray, splintery-fractured biotitic sulfidic quartz schist. Contains amphibolite, coticule, and vitreous quartzite (Ombq)

title: Moretown Formation, Quartz schist member
description: Bluish-black, rusty weathering, fine-grained albite-sericite-chlorite-quartz schist with pyrite

title: Moretown Formation, Quartzite member
description: Dark-gray to steel-bluish-gray vitreous quartzite in beds as much as 10 m thick but commonly less than 1 m thick. Resembles quartzites of the Ottauquechee Formation (Cobq)

title: Moretown Formation, Carbonaceous schist member
description: Dark-gray, fine-grained carbonaceous biotite-muscovite-quartz (+/-garnet) phyllite and schist. Occurs west of Montpelier

title: Moretown Formation, Amphibolite and greenstone member
description: Hornblende-spotted dioritic amphibolite

title: Moretown Formation, Granofels and coticule member
description: Grayish-green, chlorite-biotite-plagioclase-quartz granofels and schist containing abundant fine layers of pinkish-gray small-garnet quartzite and coticule

title: Moretown Formation, Feldspathic quartzite member
description: Light-grayish-brown- to tan-weathering biotite-muscovite feldspathic quartzite and muscovitic quartz schist

title: Moretown Formation, Chlorite schist member
description: Pale-greenish-gray, lustrous and nonlustrous chlorite-muscovite feldspathic schist and schistose granofels. Local richly garnetiferous variant (Omgt)

title: Moretown Formation, Felsic metavolcanic member
description: Gray, purplish-gray, and light-gray dacitic to andesitic metavolcanic and metavolcaniclastic rocks, similar to Omwhv

title: Moretown Formation, Garnet schist member
description: Greenish-gray feldspathic garnet schist, grades into Omfs

title: Moretown Formation, Harlow Bridge quartzite member
description: Buff-weathering, tan to green, fine-grained massive to thinly bedded quartzite intercalated with green phyllite and schist

title: Moretown Formation, Hornblende fascicule schist and granofels member
description: Light-gray to grayish-green chlorite-muscovite-biotite-plagioclase-quartz schist, conspicuous sprays of hornblende, and biotite-hornblende-plagioclase granofels

title: Middlebury Limestone
description: Buff-streaked, dark-bluish-gray, thinly bedded and well-foliated dolomitic limestone, shown above the Champlain thrust south of Middlebury

title: Morses Line Slate
description: Medium-gray to black calcareous slate

title: Mount Merino Formation
description: Light-gray, powdery-weathering, and red, green and dark-gray, thinly bedded siliceous argillite and mudstone distinguished from the Indian River Slate by abundance of cherty siliceous layers

title: Moretown Formation, Pinstriped granofels member
description: Light-gray to pale-green, whitish-gray-weathering, chlorite-biotite-plagioclase-quartz granofels and tectonically pinstriped granofels and feldspathic biotite quartzite

title: Moretown Formation, Interbedded quartzite and phyllite member
description: Light-gray laminated quartzite and vitreous quartzite interbedded with gray phyllite and schist

title: Moretown Formation, Mariposite-bearing metarondingite member
description: Bright-green and white, fine- to medium-grained, variably foliated calcite-quartz-albite-mariposite-actinolite-tremolite-epidote-zoisite granofels to gneiss. Associated with greenstone and ultramafic rocks in Roxbury

title: Moretown Formation, Truland Brook member
description: Light-gray to tan, fine-grained albite-chlorite-sericite-quartz phyllitic quartzite interlayered with light-greenish-gray quartzo-feldspathic granofels and dark-gray phyllite. Contains dark-green metamorphosed mafic dikes and sills

title: Moretown Formation, Whetstone Hill Member - Phyllite facies
description: Predominantly medium-dark-gray to lustrous-tan, fine-grained garnet-biotite-muscovite phyllite and carbonaceous phyllite, contains layers of dark-gray quartzite, coticule, and ironstone locally mapped separately

title: Moretown Formation, Whetstone Hill Member - Black sulfidic carbonaceous schist facies
description: Dark-gray, sooty- and rusty-weathering, sulfidic biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist and granofels, is a lateral variant of Omwh. Contains layers of rusty-weathering amphibolite, and dark-gray quartzite

title: Moretown Formation, Whetstone Hill Member - Metasiltstone facies
description: Pale-greenish-gray, finely laminated, magnetite-chlorite-biotite feldspathic metasiltstone and pale-greenish-yellow-weathering muscovite-chlorite-quartz phyllite

title: Moretown Formation, Whetstone Hill Member - Coticule and quartzite facies
description: Dark-gray to light-gray, vitreous magnetite quartzite, and coticule

title: Moretown Formation, Whetstone Hill Member - Metavolcanic facies
description: Pale-tannish-gray- to purplish-gray-weathering, phyllitic metadacitic volcanic breccia, agglomerate, and grayish-green fragmental meta-andesitic breccia, may occur at several levels

title: Barnard Gneiss
description: Predominantly light-gray to whitish-weathering, massive to gneissic hornblende-biotite tonalite and biotite-muscovite-quartz-plagioclase trondhjemite, includes rare hornblendite, metadiabase, and metapyroxenite

title: Mixed felsic and mafic rocks
description: Heterogeneous composite intrusive well-layered unit consisting of biotite and hornblende metatrondhjemite, garnet-hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite, and metadiabase dikes

title: South Pond facies
description: Light- to dark-gray and steel-blue to apple-green, fine-grained hornblende-chlorite-plagioclase amphibolite, locally containing significant calcite and pyrite and interlayered felsic layers of metatrondhjemite or metadacite

title: Whitneyville facies
description: Light-green to medium-green, massive, epidote-ilmenite-sphene-chlorite-hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite, marked by coarse hornblende and abundant phenocrysts of plagioclase

title: Williamsville facies
description: Dark-gray to black, poorly layered, porphyritic and nonporphyritic ilmenite-epidote-chlorite-plagioclase-hornblende amphibolite

title: Newfane tonalite
description: Light-gray to cream-weathering, massive to gneissic, hornblende-biotite and muscovite-biotite metatrondhjemite and metatonalite, forms a thick sill-like intrusive

title: Ruger Hill facies
description: Heterogeneous composite intrusive well-layered unit consisting of biotite and hornblende metatrondhjemite, garnet-hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite, and metadiabase dikes

title: Tonalite gneiss
description: Medium-grayish-green, medium-grained hornblende-biotite tonalite gneiss, with minor amphibolite

title: Metatrondhjemite and metatonalite
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray, coarse-grained muscovite-biotite-quartz-plagioclase metatrondhjemite on the east flank of the Chester dome, similar to Onb, Onnt and Ontw

title: West Halifax Trondhjemite
description: Cream-colored, light-gray- to whitish-gray-weathering, coarse-grained chlorite-biotite-muscovite-quartz-plagioclase (+/-garnet+/-hornblende) metatrondhjemite and metatonalite

title: Orwell Limestone
description: Dove-gray-weathering, black to dark-gray fine-grained limestone. Distinguished from the Middlebury Limestone with difficulty, especially in the area west of the Sudbury slice

title: Biotite granite
description: Pink, medium-grained muscovite-biotite-microcline-perthite granite and gneissic granite, and aplite of the Lebanon dome

title: Biotite granite, Granodioritic to quartz dioritic gneissic border phase
description: Granodioritic to quartz dioritic gneissic border phase of Oobg, perhaps in part metasomatic

title: Hornblende metagabbro
description: Dark-green, coarse-grained, well-foliated hornblende-andesine metagabbro

title: Partridge Formation, Sulfidic slate and phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to grayish-black, rusty-weathering sulfidic slate and phyllite interlayered with felsic volcanic rocks and tuffs and amphibolite

title: Partridge Formation, Amphibolite member
description: Amphibolite

title: Pawlet Formation
description: Light-gray, tan weathering, mica-speckled, massive to thin-bedded quartz-plagioclase wacke interbedded with dark gray carbonaceous slate. Conatins autoclastic chips of gray slate, fragments of volcanics and clasts of gray quartz and oligoclase

title: Providence Island Dolostone
description: Light-buff-tan weathering, massive to thick-bedded, fine-grained dark-gray dolostone, has beeswax-scored surfaces, contains thin layers of fossiliferous blue-gray limestone

title: Poultney Formation
description: Dull-white and whitish-gray-weathering, and pale-green and gray, thinly bedded to laminated slate and phyllite. Has distinctive beds, 1 cm to several centimeters thick, of siliceous argillite and metasiltstone and locally abundant thin beds of micritic black limestone

title: Partridge Formation, Metarhyolite member
description: Greenish-gray, light-bluish-gray, or medium-bluish-gray metarhyolite tuff, lapilli tuff, tuff breccia, and lava. Generally porphyritic with 5 to 20 percent plagioclase and, in some places, quartz phenocrysts and minor amphibolite

title: Shelburne Marble
description: Predominantly light-gray- to white- and bluish-gray-streaked calcite marble and massive white- and green-streaked calcite marble. Locally contains intermediate dolostone beds

title: Stony Point Formation
description: Dark-gray calcareous shale with beds of bluish-gray limestone

title: Chazy, Black River, and Trenton Limestones undifferentiated
description: Chazy, Black River, and Trenton Limestones undifferentiated - Shown locally west of the Taconic allochthon

title: Valcour Formation
description: Dark- to light-gray, fossiliferous limestone

title: Walloomsac Formation
description: Same description as Hortonville - Dark-gray siliceous shale and phyllite, contains thin beds of blue gray argillaceous limestone, minor beds of gray to tan quartzite grades into limey shales

title: West Bridgewater Formation, Black to dark-gray phyllite member
description: Black to dark-gray, sulfidic to nonsulfidic, carbonaceous, fine-grained, biotite-muscovite-quartz phyllite with pods and beds of mottled dolostone, ankeritic quartzite, and rhythmically layered gray quartzite, limestone breccia and laminated silicic phyllite

title: West Bridgewater Formation, Dark-gray and green phyllite member
description: Interbedded dark-gray and grayish green, chlorite-muscovite-quartz-knotted albitic phyllite containing pods of bluish-gray dolostone. (Correlation with West Bridgewater uncertain.) Mapped only in the area west of Granville

title: Walloomsac Formation
description: Black carbonaceous highly graptoliferous phyllite. Graptoliferous slate in The Taconic Allochthon: Black slate of Climacograptus bicornis Biozone on and west of Whipstock Hill, otherwise typical of slates of the Walloomsac Formation shown as Ow

title: Washburn Brook Formation, Metamorphosed gray siltstone
description: Metamorphosed gray siltstone, quartzite, volcanogenic chert, and ironstone, all typically containing coticule and magnetite

title: Walloomsac Formation
description: Basal limestone member

title: Ira Formation, Whipple Marble member
description: Basal limestone member - same as Oil

title: Washburn Brook Formation, Metamorphosed sedimentary breccia
description: Metamorphosed sedimentary breccia interlayered with dark-gray slate and micaceous siltstone. Clasts include Albee Formation, gray slate, coticule-bearing metasiltstone and chert, and quartz pebbles. Matrix consists of metasandstone, metasiltstone, or slate

title: Walloomsac Formation, Whipstock Breccia
description: Tectonic breccia formed in situ, contains abundant pseudo-pebbles

title: Walloomsac Formation, Sandy phyllite, granofels and cherty phyllite
description: Gray and grayish-green rocks associated with Whipstock breccia on Whipstock Hill but of uncertain correlation

title: Metadiorite to metamonzodiorite
description: Medium-gray-weathering, porphyritic dikes and sills of fine- to medium-grained hornblende-biotite diorite and quartz diorite, and coarse-grained quartz monzodiorite

title: Mount Nevis pluton, Biotite-bearing metagranodiorite, metagranite, and meta-aplite of the Mount Nevis pluton
description: Yellowish-gray to light-gray, medium- to coarse-grained magnetite-biotite-mesoperthite granodiorite and granite. Has mutually intrusive contacts with associated metadiorites

title: Clough Quartzite
description: Quartzite and quartz-cobble metaconglomerate, quartz-cobble conglomerate with abundant dark-gray phyllite matrix that resembles phyllite of the Littleton Formation

title: Clough Quartzite
description: Lower conglomerate and granofels on Skitchewaug Mountain

title: Pegmatitic metatonalite to metagabbro
description: Nonfoliated to foliated pegmatitic metatonalite to metagabbro

title: Pegmatitic metagabbro, metadiorite, and metatonalite
description: Foliated to non-foliated, fine-grained to pegmatitic metagabbro, metadiorite, and metatonalite, aplitic metatonalite, and metadiabase

title: Clough Quartzite
description: Upper quartzite on Skitchewaug Mountain

title: Shaw Mountain Formation, Basal volcaniclastic and metasedimentary member
description: Heterogeneous, thin (<10 m-thick) unit of interbedded quartzite, amphibolite, felsic granofels and phyllite occurring at the base of the Waits River Formation on the north end of the Chester dome

title: Fitch Formation
description: Metamorphosed limestone, calcareous sandstone, siltstone, and pelite. Some limestone conglomerate and polymict conglomerate with calcareous matrix

title: Greenvale Cove Formation
description: Thin-bedded muscovite-biotite-garnet-staurolite-kyanite schist and micaceous quartz-feldspar granofels, some calc-silicate lenses and layers

title: Northfield Formation, carbonaceous phyllite member
description: Dark-gray to silvery-gray, lustrous, fine-grained carbonaceous quartz-muscovite phyllite and silicic phyllite, and garnet-rich biotite-muscovite-quartz schist, contains beds of gray quartzite and metasiltstone, beds of quartz-feldspar grit or quartzite near base, and minor quartzose limestone

title: Diorite and trondhjemite
description: Metamorphosed diorite, trondhjemite, and diabase, consisting of massive to foliated, light-gray to grayish-green, chalky-weathering diorite with xenoliths of green phyllite and trondhjemite, and massive, tan-weathering, medium- to coarse-grained trondhjemite with xenoliths of diabase

title: Granodiorite
description: Tan to light-bluish-gray, brown-weathering, medium- to coarse-grained, equigranular to porphyritic foliated granodiorite composed of quartz, plagioclase, perthite, microcline, biotite, and sericite

title: Northfield Formation, carbonaceous phyllite and limestone member
description: Dark-gray to silvery-gray, carbonaceous quartz-muscovite silicic slate phyllite or schist with as much as 5 percent beds of punky limestone west of the Guilford dome

title: Northfield Formation, Quartzite, grit and conglomerate member
description: Dark-gray, quartz-pebble metawacke and gray quartzite and conglomerate at base of the Northfield Formation, south of Springfield

title: Rangeley Formation, Schist member
description: Interlayered, commonly rusty-weathering quartz-feldspar micaceous granofels and dark-gray mica schist containing porphyroblasts of garnet, staurolite, and kyanite. Calc-silicate lenses common in the granofels, granule and pebble metaconglomerate

title: Rangeley Formation, Conglomerate member
description: Quartz conglomerate

title: Rangeley Formation, Sulfidic schist member
description: Rusty sulfidic schist

title: Shaw Mountain Formation, conglomerate member
description: White to yellowish-gray, quartz-pebble conglomerate to conglomeratic quartzite with quartzite matrix and phyllitic quartzite, quartz-pebble to -granule phyllite and vitreous quartzite in beds as much as 5 m thick

title: Sawyer Mountain Formation
description: Greenish-gray to dark-gray, pyritic, locally calcareous phyllite and light-gray, locally pyritic and calcareous, fine- to medium-grained, feldspar-rich metasandstone, some beds are punky weathering. Graded grit and conglomerate beds toward base

title: Metafelsite
description: Felsic metavolcanic rocks includes volcanic debris flow, laminated tuff, and strongly foliated felsite

title: Brandon Lignite
description: Organic, silt, sand, gravel and slumped and dismembered lignite occurring as elongate disrupted deposits in underlying kaolin, residual hematite and ochre deposits near Brandon

title: Biotite-epidote-quartz gneiss and epidotic quartzite
description: Light-pale-yellowish-green to gray quartzite gneiss containing abundant epidote and locally magnetite, and frosted round grains of quartz associated with diopside-bearing quartzite

title: Biotite-quartz-plagioclase gneiss
description: A widespread heterogeneous unit of well-layered, predominantly biotite-quartz-plagioclase gneisses containing variable amounts of magnetite, hornblende, and garnet, and little potash feldspar

title: Cavendish Formation, Marble and calc-silicate member
description: Includes white, coarse-grained calcite marble, beige to gray, medium- to coarse-grained phlogopite-tremolite-dolomite-quartz-(+/-talc) marble, greenish actinolite-dolomite-calcite marble, phlogopite-diopside-scapolite-calcite-dolomite marble

title: Amphibolite
description: Dark-grayish-green, fine-grained quartz-hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite, locally garnetiferous and medium-grained hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite

title: Baileys Mills tonalitic gneiss, Tonalite gneiss
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray-weathering, medium-grained biotite-quartz-plagioclase gneiss flecked with coarse biotite. Contains numerous lenses of fine-grained amphibolite

title: Baileys Mills tonalitic gneiss, Plagioclase-phenocrystic tonalite gneiss
description: Coarse-grained facies of the Baileys Mills tonalitic gneiss exposed on the northeast flank of the Chester dome

title: Cavendish Formation, Feldspathic schist and granofels member
description: Light-gray to medium-dark-gray, rusty-weathering, white-plagioclase-spotted biotite-quartz-plagioclase granofels, massive grayish-green chlorite-spotted, magnetite-studded, biotite-plagioclase-quartz granofels and gneiss, and porphyroclastic plagioclase-augen-biotite mylonite gneiss

title: Cavendish Formation, Gassetts Schist Member
description: Lustrous, yellowish-grayish-green, ilmenite-staurolite (+/-kyanite)-garnet (large) -plagioclase-biotite-muscovite-quartz schist and warty-textured, dark-gray, biotite-rich garnet (large)-plagioclase-quartz schist, local granofels with chlorite pseudomorphs after garnet

title: Cavendish Formation, Marble and calc-silicate member
description: Coarse-grained dark-green diopside (+/-hornblende+/-zoisite)-calc-silicate rocks, white talc-tremolite (+/-dolomite)-calc-silicate schist, and minor quartzite, diopside quartzite, and schistose bluish-gray marble

title: Hornblende diorite gneiss
description: Coarse-grained hornblende-plagioclase (+/-quartz) dioritic gneiss and gabbroic gneiss mapped in the Londonderry area, where it is interpreted as metagabbro

title: Felchville Gneiss, Felchville trondhjemite facies
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray-weathering, magnetite-biotite-microcline-quartz-plagioclase metatrondhjemite to granodioritic gneiss. Intrudes paragneiss units of the Chester dome

title: Felchville Gneiss, Felchville aplitic facies
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray, fine-grained, magnetite trondhjemitic gneiss and aplitic trondhjemite, intricately intrusive into layered paragneisses of the Chester dome. Contains xenoliths of more mafic gneiss

title: Quartzite, undifferentiated
description: Tan to rusty brown or gray thinly layered garnet-biotite-quartzite and schistose quartzite associated with aluminous schists, calc-silicate rocks or interbedded within biotite-quartz-plagioclase paragneiss

title: Quartz schist
description: Rusty-weathering sulfidic schist and minor amphibolite older than part of the South Londonderry Igneous Suite

title: Rawsonville trondhjemite gneiss
description: Chalky-white to light-gray-weathering, medium- to coarse-grained biotite metatrondhjemite and aplite (Y1rta)

title: Rawsonville trondhjemite gneiss
description: Aplite in Y1rt

title: Tonalite gneiss
description: Medium-gray- to light-gray-weathering, biotite (+/-hornblende) tonalite gneiss exposed on Torment Hill in Weston

title: Amphibolite
description: Dark-grayish-green, fine-grained quartz-hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite, locally garnetiferous and medium-grained hornblende-plagioclase amphibolite

title: Aplitic gneiss
description: Light-gray to white, fine-grained aplitic granite gneiss as border of Y2gg or thin dikes or sills in paragneiss units

title: Mafic gneiss
description: Mafic gneiss

title: Aluminous schist and gneiss, Quartz schist and gneiss
description: Steel-gray-weathering, garnet (small)-quartz-biotite gneiss and quartzite

title: Mafic gneiss
description: Dark-gray to black, fine-grained, magnetite-garnet-hornblende-biotite-diopside-plagioclase gneiss, commonly containing beds of quartzite, tremolite-pyroxene gneiss, schist, and sulfidic quartzite

title: Biotite-plagioclase quartz gneiss
description: Light-greenish-gray to pinkish-gray well-foliated, and well-layered quartz-rich gneiss and more mafic biotite-hornblende-pyroxene-quartz-plagioclase gneiss irregularly distributed within unit

title: Biotite tonalite gneiss
description: Predominantly chalky-white weathering, massive biotite tonalite gneiss having screens, dikes, or sills of more mafic gneiss. Passes laterally into white, fine-grained trondhjemitic aplite near contacts with larger screens of paragneiss

title: Bondville metadacite and trondhjemite gneiss
description: Light-gray to whitish-gray, fine-grained biotite trondhjemitic gneiss, locally containing abundant magnetite

title: College Hill Granite Gneiss
description: Light-gray to medium-dark-gray, porphyritic biotite-microcline-perthite granodioritic gneiss and pegmatite. Strongly deformed, lineated and saturated with less deformed later pegmatite, migmatitic border exhibits fewer microcline megacrysts

title: Cole Pond tonalite gneiss
description: Gray to medium-dark-gray, biotite-rich metatonalite gneiss, having irregular screens, and xenoliths of more mafic hornblende-biotite tonalite or diorite gneiss

title: Marble and calc-silicate gneiss
description: Medium-dark-gray to light-gray diopside-phlogopite-scapolite-calcite marble, phlogopite-tremolite-talc schist, and dark-gray diopside-hornblende (actinolite)-plagioclase calc-silicate gneiss

title: Dolomite marble
description: Light-gray to yellowish-gray, coarse-grained dolomite-phlogopite-scapolite marble, pyritiferous varieties weather salmon pink to beige. Commonly associated with tremolite-talc marble and tremolite-talc schist

title: Biotite-granitic gneiss
description: A heterogeneous unit consisting of granitic and granodioritic and aplite biotitic microcline-rich gneisses, highly gneissic and locally migmatitic occurring in the southern part of the Green Mountain massif

title: Hornblende-plagioclase gneiss
description: Medium- to coarse-grained hornblende dioritic-appearing gneiss

title: Hague Gneiss
description: Yellowish-grayish-green to rusty-sulfidic-weathering, garnet-sillimanite-biotite-orthoclase-plagioclase-quartz schist or gneiss, locally containing mappable and discontinuous lenses, layers or pods of quartzite, marble, or calc-silicate rock

title: Granitic gneiss of Lincoln Mountain massif
description: Heterogeneous unit consists of medium-grained biotite-microcline-plagioclase gneiss and pinkish-gray, medium- to coarse-grained and microcline-perthite granitic gneiss. Interpreted as intrusive granitic rock older than Y3 rocks of Chittenden Intrusive Suite

title: Ludlow Mountain aplitic gneiss
description: Light-gray to white, very fine grained microcline-plagioclase-quartz (+/-magnetite) aplitic gneiss contains sparing amounts of biotite, and secondary muscovite. Unit interpreted as a border facies of Y2lgg

title: Ludlow Mountain granodiorite gneiss
description: Light-gray, medium- to fine-grained garnet-biotite-microcline-perthite granodiorite, magnetite-studded white aplite, and kyanite-tourmaline pegmatite. Contains 0.5-cm clots of muscovite possibly after beryl

title: Okemo Quartzite
description: Light-tan to whitish-gray, massive vitreous quartzite in beds several meters thick, interlayered with rusty-grayish-brown garnet-muscovitic quartzite and aluminous sericite-muscovite-tourmaline retrograde phyllite

title: Calcite marble
description: Light blue-gray and white coarse-grained and medium-grained calcite diopside marble calcite-diopside-talc marble in beds or pods less than 5 m thick, interbedded with or passes laterally into other calc-silicate rock

title: Migmatitic and mylonitic rocks of uncertain origin, Migmatitic gneiss
description: Light-gray and pinkish-gray to yellowish-gray, massive, medium-grained plagioclase granitic gneiss and migmatite-veined biotite plagioclase gneiss. A mixed rock of uncertain origin

title: Migmatitic and mylonitic rocks of uncertain origin, Mylonitic gneiss
description: Highly schistose, biotite-muscovite (+/-chlorite) feldspathic mylonite and mylonitic gneiss mapped near Brandon Gap and in the Pine Hill slice west of Wallingford as Yur

title: Proctor Hill granodiorite gneiss
description: Aplitic and hornblende-rich reaction zones where granodiorite gneiss of Y2phg is in contact with calc-silicate rocks

title: Proctor Hill granodiorite gneiss
description: Gray to pinkishgray, gneissoid magnetite-biotite-microcline-perthite granodiorite, and locally microcline megacrystic gneissic granite, well-foliated and highly variable in composition

title: Quartzite, undifferentiated
description: Tan to rusty brown or gray thinly layered garnet-biotite-quartzite and schistose quartzite associated with aluminous schists, calc-silicate rocks or interbedded within biotite-quartz-plagioclase paragneiss

title: Quartzite
description: Light-tan to yellowish-gray, massive to well-layered magnetite-garnet quartzite and magnetite-biotite-garnet quartzite in beds as much as 10 m thick

title: Garnet-biotite gneiss
description: Dark-gray- to rusty-grayish-brown-weathering, sulfidic muscovite-biotite-magnetite gneiss or schist marked by abundant small garnets, biotite, and fine laminae of quartz and plagioclase. Contains thin belts of amphibolite and calc-silicate gneiss

title: Aluminous schist and gneiss, Quartz schist and gneiss
description: Tan garnet-muscovite-biotite-quartz-plagioclase gneiss and rusty schist, locally containing abundant chloritized garnet, lustrous yellowish-grayish-green phyllonitic retrograde varieties contain chloritoid-chlorite and relict garnet (red dot overprint)

title: Carbonaceous sulfidic schist
description: Dark-gray, rusty-weathering carbonaceous to graphitic schist associated with quartzite and calc-silicate rock near Killington

title: Aluminous schist and gneiss, Washington Gneiss
description: Dark-rusty-grayish-brown-weathering, graphitic garnet-plagioclase-biotite-quartz (+/-sillimanite) schist, rusty-weathering blue-quartz-ribbed quartz schist, garnet quartzite and rusty-weathering layers of sulfidic calc-silicate rock

title: Wilcox Formation, Calc-silicate gneiss and marble member
description: Dark-green, massive, diopside-hornblende rock, lenses of bluish-gray to gray, medium- to coarse-grained calcite marble and calcite-diopside marble and dolomitic talc-phlogopite-tremolite schist

title: Wilcox Formation, Dolomite marble member
description: Beige-weathering to whitish-gray, fine-grained dolomite marble

title: Wilcox Formation, Garnetiferous quartzite and quartz schist member
description: Lustrous muscovite-chlorite-chloritoid or muscovite-chlorite-biotite-clinozoisite retrograde schistose quartzite and large-garnet schist. Resembles a retrograde variety of the Hague Gneiss (of Alling, 1918) (Y2hgn) near Whitehall, NY

title: Wilcox Formation, Quartzite member
description: Tan, yellow-gray weathering garnet-muscovite-quartzite and feldspathic retrograde garnet quartz gneiss

title: Wilcox Formation
description: Lustrous to rusty weathering biotite-muscovite+/-chloritoid and retrograde coarse-garnet schist

title: Altered rocks adjacent to the Chittenden Intrusive Suite, Albite-magnetite studded gneiss
description: Gray or greenish-gray, albite- and magnetite-studded granulose biotite-quartz-plagioclase gneiss, containing chloritized biotite and garnet. Occurs as altered varieties of Y1,2bg near Y3Ama

title: Granulose albitic gneiss
description: Massive, lineated, light-tannish-gray to gray-green, medium-grained, granulose, epidote-magnetite-biotite (chlorite)-muscovite-albite-quartz gneiss, veined with magnetite, spots of ankerite, clots of chlorite after original amphibole, pyroxene or garnet

title: Microcline-augen granite and monzogranite gneiss
description: More equigranular granitic gneiss than Y3Ama with which it passes locally into

title: Metagabbro
description: Garnet-hornblende (+/-olivine) gabbro and dioritic gneiss and biotite-hornblende (+/-pyroxene) gabbro and diorite

title: Granodioritic augen gneiss and quartz monzonite gneiss
description: Light-gray to pinkish-gray, garnet-biotite-plagioclase-microperthite augen granodioritic gneiss, locally massive but well foliated. Contains deformed phenocrysts (augen) aligned in old relict flow(?) foliation

title: Granitic gneiss of Chittenden Intrusive Suite (?)
description: Light-gray, coarse-grained, biotite-microcline megacrystic to even-grained granite gneiss closely associated with 1149- Ma to 1120-Ma augen gneisses, in the northern part of the Green Mountain massif

title: Microcline augen gneiss of Lincoln Mountain massif
description: Light- to medium-gray, medium-grained, biotite-quartz-plagioclase-microcline gneiss, contains microcline augen as much as 4 cm in length

title: Microcline-augen granite and monzogranite gneiss
description: Gray to whitish-gray, coarse-grained biotite-microcline megacrystic granite and monzogranitic gneiss. Enclaves of paragneiss are locally albitized and enriched in magnetite. Enclaves of altered aluminous rocks with restites of chloritoid and sericite

title: Microcline-magnetite augen gneiss at Brandon Gap
description: Pinkish-gray to medium-dark-gray, biotite-magnetite-microcline-plagioclase augen gneiss. Unit is associated with minor exposures of metadiorite to tonalitic gneisses

title: Granite pegmatite and pegmatoid granite
description: Pinkish-gray to light-gray, biotite (+/-muscovite+/-tourmaline+/-magnetite) pegmatite and pegmatoid granite associated with augen gneisses of Chittenden Intrusive Suite, in Brandon

title: Microcline-augen granite and monzogranite gneiss
description: Biotite pegmatoid granitic gneiss locally muscovite-bearing

title: Pharoah Mountain Gneiss
description: Rusty-grayish-brown- to brown-weathering, knubbly coarse-grained magnetite-garnet-hornblende and pyroxene-bearing charnockitic gneiss and garnet-hornblende granite gneiss

title: Albitic biotite granite and pegmatite at Baker Brook
description: Light-gray biotite granite gneiss containing abundant rose-colored zircon confined to the Pine Hill slice

title: Albitic biotite granite and pegmatite at Baker Brook
description: Pinkish-gray garnet-biotite-albite pegmatite and granitic augen gneiss, distinguished by abundant rose-colored zircon

title: Somerset Reservoir Granite
description: White to pinkish gray, medium-grained plagioclase-microcline-perthite aplitic to pegmatitic granite forms dikes in country rocks and irregular border facies

title: Bull Hill Gneiss
description: Light-pinkish-gray to gray, very coarse grained to medium-grained and mylonitic biotite-plagioclase-quartz-microcline augen gneiss, locally has large ovoidal relict microcline with rapakivi rims and intrusive breccia

title: Harriman Reservoir Granite
description: Light-gray to pinkish gray, biotite-plagioclase-microcline megacrystic granite and augen gneiss, rapakivi texture locally preserved, occurs in the Rayponda and Sadawga domes

title: Stamford Granite
description: Light-gray to medium-gray, very coarse grained biotite-plagioclase-microcline rapakivi granite, contains large megacrysts of microcline perthite having rims of plagioclase that contain inclusions of biotite and garnet

title: Stamford Granite
description: Fine-grained facies consisting of white-weathering, muscovite-biotite-microcline-plagioclase aplitic granite locally forms a border facies or thin internal dikes

title: Somerset Reservoir Granite
description: Light-gray to pinkish-gray, biotite-plagioclase-microcline megacrystic granite and augen gneiss, rapakivi texture locally preserved. Unit occurs in the Rayponda and Sadawga domes

title: Pegmatite
description: Light-gray to pinkish-gray, biotite-muscovite (+/-garnet+/-tourmaline+/-magnetite) granite pegmatite as crosscutting pods and larger bodies. Albitic garnet-muscovite pegmatite common

title: Problematic rocks at Devils Den in Weston and Danby areas (Mesoproterozoic?), Muscovite-chlorite-garnet schist
description: Light-silvery-green to grayish-green, lustrous muscovite-chlorite-quartz (+/-garnet+/-chloritoid+/-ilmenite) schist and biotite-albite-muscovite-quartz schist

title: Problematic rocks at Devils Den in Weston and Danby areas (Mesoproterozoic?), Dolomite marble
description: Beige to pinkish-gray-weathering, pyrite-bearing, medium- and fine-grained phlogopite-chlorite-dolomite marble exposed in cliffs east of the road at Devils Den

title: Problematic rocks at Devils Den in Weston and Danby areas (Mesoproterozoic?), Biotite-muscovite-plagioclase-quartz schist
description: A highly heterogeneous unit, distinguished from Y?cms by its generally rusty-weathering, nonlustrous appearance and by the abundance of large albite crystals, conspicuous large plates of muscovite and biotite, and abundant clinozoisite

title: Problematic rocks at Devils Den in Weston and Danby areas (Mesoproterozoic?), Quartzite
description: Light-gray to pinkish-gray, magnetite-muscovite-plagioclase quartzite at Devils Den

title: Aluminous schist and gneiss, Retrograde gneiss
description: Retrograde aluminous gness shown above Pine Hill thrust near South Wallingford. See also Y2myu

title: Mafic dikes
description: Medium- to coarse-grained, foliated, actinolite-chlorite-calcite-epidote retrograded metadiabasic dikes, commonly have relict diabasic texture

title: Diabase dike
description: Dark-gray to greenish-gray, very fine grained, ocellar basaltic to medium-grained augite-plagioclase diabasic dikes, occurring as subvertical northeast trending discontinuous zone in the center of Bald Mountain

title: Bull West Castleton and Hatch Hill Formations, dolostone member
description: Pods, lenses or zones of thinly bedded dolostone

title: Bull West Castleton and Hatch Hill Formations, limestone member
description: Pods, lenses or zones of thinly bedded limestone and limestone conglomerate
